input_scope: Source narrative and rival submissions; target decisive reasoning/outcome excluded. Existing lower-court findings retained with level. A quoted lease term may be included separately from the target analysis introducing it.
coverage_limits: Retrospective source-conditioned retrieval, not pre-litigation prediction.
Eligibility review is not complete semantic annotation.

segments.text: APPLICATION FOR EVICTION OF TENANT UNDER
SECTION 14 (1) (b) OF  THE DELHI RENT CONTROL
JUDGMENT

Vide this order, the application under cite8†section 14 (1) (b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act 59 of 1958") made by the petitioners against respondent/tenant for eviction is disposed off. The brief and relevant facts for disposal of the application is mentioned as below:­ 2 As stated, the premises i.e. G­45, Connaught Circus, New E. No. 2/11 Page no.2 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.

Delhi­11001(hereinafter called the tenanted premises), as shown in red colour in the site plan attached with the petition was let out vide lease deed dated 19.8.1991 to the respondent M/s Gill & Co consisting of two partners i.e. Sh Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Sh Ashok Kumar Bhasin, both sons of Late Sh Madan Mohan Bhasin, for commercial purposes. It is further stated that the premises was let out by the landlords consisting of Sh Rajdev Singh, petitioner no1, petitioner no.

2 and Sh Gopal Inder Singh; that Sh Rajdev Singh, father of petitioner no. 1 died in the year 2002; that rights of father of petitioner no. 1 in the tenanted premises were inherited by petitioner no. 1.; that Sh Gopal Inder Singh sold his share in the tenanted property to M/s Atma Ram Properties Pvt. Ltd, i.e. petitioner no. 2 and as such the petitioner no. 1 to 3 are the owners/landlords of the tenanted premises.

It is averred that none of the partners of the respondent who constituted the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co at the time of inception of tenancy are now the partner of the respondent no. 1 and none of the said partners is in actual possession or legal possession of the tenanted premises. It is averred that Sh. Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Sh Ashok Kumar Bhasin have illegally and unauthorizedly sublet, assigned and parted with the possession of the E. No. 2/11 Page no.3 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.

tenanted premises to Sh. Ramesh Tewari and Sh Rajan Tewari, who constituted M/s Gill & Co and are in occupation of the entire shop. Therefore this application is filed by the petitioners against the respondent praying for passing eviction order under cite8†section 14(1)(b) of the DRC Act qua the tenanted premises.

3 After service of the process, written statement was filed by the respondent contending that the respondent is a partnership firm duly registered with Registrar of Firms vide registration No. 447 dated 8.2.2010 and it consists of four partners as mentioned in the Form A issued by the Registrar of Firms under cite9†section 59(4) (1) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932. The contention of the petitioners that the constitution of respondent firm has changed which created a ground for eviction is false.

It is stated that change in constitution of partnership firm does not amount to change in tenancy and even otherwise the respondent firm still consists of partners who had taken the premises in question on rent. As contended, this ground is not available to the petitioners and the petition deserves dismissal. However, it is not disputed that the premises were let out by the erstwhile owners vide lease deed dated 19.8.1991.
As further contended that the site plan filed by the petitioners is not correct and E. No. 2/11 Page no.4 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.

in accordance to the site which had been made a part of lease deed dated 19.8.1991. It is denied that the tenant has sublet, assigned or parted with possession of the tenanted shop as alleged. It is stated that at the time of inception of tenancy, the firm M/s Gill & Co consisted of four partners and the same partners continue to be the partners of the firm. Mr.

Rajan Tiwari was one of the partners at the commencement of tenancy on 19.8.1991; that the premises were let out to the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co and not to any individual partners in his individual capacity as tenant and the possession of the tenanted premises is still with the firm, i.e. M/s Gill & Co. As contended, the petitioners are not entitled to any relief and prayed that the petition be dismissed with cost.

4 To the written statement of the respondent, the petitioners filed replication wherein the averments made in the application for eviction are reiterated and the defence taken by the respondent are traversed.

5 In support of their case, the applicant/petitioner no. 1 filed her affidavit Ex. P­1 by way of evidence and examined herself as PW1. The witness deposed that she alongwith petitioners no. 2 and 3 is the owner and landlord of the tenanted premises and all the three E. No. 2/11 Page no.5 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.

petitioners have executed a power of attorney Ex. PW1/1 in favour of Sh. Mohan Chandra Dhyani. She further deposed in her affidavit that the tenanted premises which is shown in red colour in the site plan Ex. PW1/2 were leased out to partners i.e. Sh Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Sh Ashok Kumar Bhasin, constituting firm M/s Gill & Co vide lease deed dated 19.8.1991 Ex. PW1/3 by the erstwhile owners and the site plan of the tenanted premises appended forms the part of the said lease deed.

She further deposed that at the time of execution of the lease deed only a part "A" of the leased premises was in occupation of M/s Gill & Co as the legal subtenant of earlier tenant Mr. C. Christopher in respect of part "A" of G­45, Ground Floor, Connaught Place, New Delhi and it is only after execution of lease deed Ex.

PW1/3 that the respondent became the tenant of the entire G­45, Ground Floor, Connaught Place, New Delhi and their status of sub­tenant in respect of part "A" of the premises also changed from sub­tenant to tenant of the petitioners; that the premises were let for non­residential purposes and are being used for commercial purpose. The witness further stated in her affidavit Ex.

P­1 that at the time when the tenanted premises were leased out, only Sh Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Sh Ashok Kumar Bhasin constituted the tenant firm M/s E. No. 2/11 Page no.6 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.

Gill & Co and the rent of the tenanted premises till December has been tendered by them. It is further stated by the witness in her affidavit Ex. P­1 that at present, none of the partners, who were the partners of M/s Gill & Co at he time of inception of tenancy, are now the partners of the entity and the earlier partners have illegally sublet, assigned and parted with possession of the tenanted premises to some new partners i.e.

Sh Rajan Tewari and Sh Ramesh Tiwari; that neither Sh Rajan Tewari nor Sh Ramesh Tiwari are the tenant of the respondent or any of the landlords. They are illegal occupant of the tenanted premises. The witness has also filed and proved on record certified copies of DR No. 84/10 titled M/s Gill &Co v Alape Kaur, reply and rejoinder as Ex. PW1/4 to Ex. PW1/6. The witness further reiterated/produced the averments as mentioned in the petition.
As no other witness remained to be examined by the petitioner the PE was closed.

6 Sh. Naresh Kumar Bhasin, one of the partners of the respondent, filed his affidavit by way of evidence and was examined as RW1. The witness has deposed that the premises was let out to respondent, a partnership firm, vide partnership deed dated 17.8.1991 Ex. RW1/A. The witness further deposed in his affidavit that lease E. No. 2/11 Page no.7 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.

deed Ex. RW1/A had been executed between the then owners of the leased property and the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co which consisted of four partners as mentioned in the partnership deed dated 17.8.1991 Ex. RW1A. The witness proved the Forms A and B issued by the office of Registrar of Firms as Ex. RW1/F and RW1/G.; that on 5.12.1991 a current no. 4351 (53001100000894 new account number) had been opened by the respondent with The Vysya Bank Ltd ( now ING Vysya Bank Ltd) Karol Bagh Branch, New Delhi.

The witness has proved the account opening form, undertaking and letter of partnership all dated 5.12.1991 as Ex. RW1/B1 to B3 and also letter dated 26.4.2011 written to the ban and reply 27.4.2011 of the bank as Ex. RW1/D. The witness has also proved copies of the three cheques dated 23.4.1997, 16.9.1997 and 21.5.99 Ex. RW1/E­1 to E3 regarding payment of rent of premises to the father of petitioner no. 1. The witness further deposed that the petitioners no.

1 to 3 were well aware about the constituent partners of respondent firm before the lease deed dated 19.8.1991 was registered by them and the present petition filed by the petitioners is false and frivolous and the same has been filed on flimsy grounds; that the site plan as annexed to the petition is not correct and not in accordance to the site plan which had been E. No. 2/11 Page no.8 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.
made a part of lease deed dated 19.8.1991.

7 Sh. Ramesh Tiwari filed his affidavit Ex. R­1 and examined himself as RW2. The witness The witness in one way or the other supported the case of the respondent and corroborated the statement of RW1 on all material facts. As no other witness remained to be examined by the respondents, the RE was closed. 8 I have heard counsel for the parties and have gone through the relevant materials on record.
I have also gone through the judgments relied by the parties in support of claim and contentions alongwith the written submissions filed.

9 The petitioners have filed written arguments relying upon authorities in support of their claim and contentions. It is argued that the suit premises was let out to the partnership firm M/s Gill & Co consisting two partners namely, Naresh Kumar Bhasin and Ashok Kumar Bhasin and none of the partners who constituted the partnership firm at the time of inception of tenancy are the partner now. It is further contended that the earlier partners have unauthorizedly sublet the premises.
The petitioner have relied upon the following judgments in support of their contentions:­
E. No. 2/11                                                                                                     Page no.9 of 23
Alape Kaur  etc vs Gill & Co.
iv) (2005) 1 SCC 31; and

Ld. Counsel for the petitioners has further argued that in view of testimony of PW­1, the documents and above reported judgments relied upon by them, the case of the petitioners is categorically proved and prayed to pass an eviction order in favour of the petitioners in view of the provisions of Clause (b) of proviso to sub­cite10†section 1 of cite11†section 14 of the Act 59 of 1958. 10 Ld.

Counsel for the respondent on the other hand argued that this petition is filed without any basis and the suit premises is still in possession of the respondent/partnership firm M/s Gill & Co. and the contention of the petitioners regarding subletting has no substance. There is no admission by the respondent at all as mentioned in the petition and M/s Gill & Co. has four partners contrary to the contention of the petitioners. Ld.

Counsel for the respondent has further relied upon testimony of the RWs alongwith the documents on record contending that the premises has never been E. No. 2/11 Page no.10 of 23 Alape Kaur etc vs Gill & Co.
sub­let . The respondent has also relied upon the judgments as mentioned below:­
ii) AIR 1967 SC 1134;
v) AIR 1992 Delhi 295; and
vi) AIR 1998 All. 220, contending that the petitioners have failed to prove their case and the petition be dismissed with heavy cost.
